problem: Two tables described one concept. taxonomy::score::MODULE_WEIGHTS (Accessibility 35, Performance 20, SEO 20, Security 15, Mobile 10) had no caller anywhere in src/ and contradicted the weights actually used, which were six inline literals in audit::normalized::build_module_scores (Accessibility 40, Performance 20, SEO 15, Security 10, Mobile 10, HTML Conformance 5). The only use of the dead table was a test asserting its entries sum to 100 — a green test guarding a model that never ran. Separately, overall_score is divided by the weight of the *contributing* modules, so a module that was skipped or could not measure silently changed the denominator rather than the result, and nothing in the report or the JSON said so.
evidence: grep over src/ for MODULE_WEIGHTS and weight_for found no caller outside src/taxonomy/score.rs itself (2026-09-19, auditmysite v1.5.0). For the renormalisation: `auditmysite https://www.casoon.de --full` reports overall_score 92 on a weight basis of 100, while `--full --skip-performance` reports 95 on a basis of 80 — the same grade, label and rating on a different basis, with nothing distinguishing them. Note that the plan's original premise no longer reproduced: without --full all six weighted modules still contribute, so overall_score == accessibility_score does not occur; only a skipped or unmeasurable weighted module triggers it (Performance, #QA-023).
expected: One table: MODULE_WEIGHTS carries the live weights keyed by the canonical module names, and build_module_scores reads them through module_weight(name) rather than repeating literals. The weight basis is published as summary.overall_score_weight_basis and stated in the PDF whenever it is below 100, naming the excluded modules — derived from the weight table, not from the module entry list, since a skipped module has no entry at all. In batch mode the published basis is the lowest across the audited pages so it never overstates the backing, and overall_score_weight_basis_uniform reports whether the pages agreed.
counter_examples: Indicator modules (UX, Journey, AI Visibility, …) must keep weight 0 and stay out of the table — they never fed the overall score; see module_weight_is_zero_for_modules_outside_the_overall_score.
A complete run must not show the weight-basis note: it only fires below 100, so a full audit reads exactly as before.
Excluding an unmeasurable Performance module from the weighted score stays correct (#QA-023) — the fix discloses the renormalisation, it does not stop it.
